newsitem.title: UK: National Power sees increased competition.
newsitem.headline: National Power sees increased competition.

text.p: British electricity generator National Power Plc said on Wednesday it expected competition to intensify in the UK but said it was aiming for real dividend growth.

The company said year pre-tax profits before exceptionals totalled 740 million pounds, down eight percent from a year ago. It paid out a dividend of 25 pence per share, compared with 23 pence previously.

National Power said trading in the early part of the current year was in line and added that earnings from overseas would continue to grow and over the longer term, "offset the forecast UK decline and...lead to resumed growth".

National Power said it did not believe it should be subjected to a one-off windfall tax which is planned by the new Labour government because it operates in an open market and "does not believe there is any evidence to show it has made excess profits."
Labour has said it will introduce the tax, aimed at funding a three billion pound programme to cut unemployment, on the "excess profits" of privatised utilities but has given no details.

National Power paid out a special dividend of one pound per share at annual results in 1996, after it was blocked from buying a regional electricity company, with a robust gain in pre-tax profits to 806 million pounds from 705 million previously.
